**#235 relaxed everything except commit.** It split the guard into three tiers and put `git commit` alone in Tier 1b — hard denial, never a prompt. From the source:

`scripts/agents/agent-worktree-guard.common.ps1:1299-1304`

```
# Commit dominates regardless of scan order. ... Approving an Ask here would let the

$isTier1b = $commitBlocks
```

Verified core claims on this machine. Verdict: **premise sound, boundary real, but design over-scoped and has three holes.**

## What I proved

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| Windows sandbox actually denies writes | **True.** `codex sandbox -P read-only ... Set-Content marker.txt` → `Access to the path ... is denied`, no file created. Probe ran inside `%TEMP%`, so temp is not implicitly writable |
| `--sandbox read-only`, `--ephemeral`, `--ignore-user-config`, `--strict-config`, `-C` parse before `review` | True — `codex exec --sandbox read-only -C . review --help` exits 0 |
| `codex exec review` has `--base`, `--commit`, `--uncommitted` | True |
| Cited `file:line` evidence (AGENTS.md 274-276, guard 674/700, README 38-46, hooks.json, config.toml) | All accurate |
| Clone cost | `.git` = 9.6 MB. `--no-hardlinks` clone cheap. Working tree 5.5 GB but that's ignored `bin/obj/node_modules` |

## Real holes

**1. MCP servers escape the sandbox.** `--ignore-user-config` drops only `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`. Project `.codex/config.toml` still loads from `--cd`, and it enables MudBlazor MCP with `default_tools_approval_mode = "auto"`. MCP server processes run outside the sandboxed shell. Design says "no writable MCP or connector configuration" but never says how. Needs explicit `-c mcp_servers={}` plus `--ignore-rules`, and `.codex/hooks.json` in the snapshot needs handling too (hook trust).

**2. Snapshot supplies its own config — self-trust loop.** For `-Uncommitted`, the snapshot contains the author's uncommitted `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json`. Reviewing a branch that changes Codex config means the reviewer runs under config written by the code under review. Fix: strip or override agent config in the snapshot before start.

**3. Preflight as written is not implementable.** `codex sandbox` in 0.144.5 **requires** `--permission-profile`, needs a `[permissions]` table, and has no `--ignore-user-config`. My working probe was `-P read-only -c 'permissions.read-only={sandbox_mode="read-only"}'`. Design's preflight steps 1-6 assume flags that do not exist on that subcommand. Also 0.146.0 already released — this surface churns. Add a version floor check plus the exact preflight command.

**4. `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` will probably not reach the reviewer.** Design says "the process inherits" it. Codex filters child env via `shell_environment_policy`; default inherit is not "all". Set it explicitly: `-c shell_environment_policy.set.GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS="0"`.

## Wrong claim

> An ordinary subagent ... inherits the parent session's effective permissions.

Not true for Claude Code subagents with an explicit `tools:` list. `cavecrew-reviewer` is `Read, Grep, Bash`. Conclusion still holds — Bash can write — but the stated reason is wrong, and it matters, because it hides the cheap fix: a reviewer agent with `Read, Grep, Glob` and no Bash cannot write at all.

## Over-scoped

Review classification pulls in "review a plan or specification" and "investigate whether reported findings are valid". Under this policy, **this very review** would have been illegal. Reading a markdown file and answering is not the failure mode. The failure was a write-capable agent turned loose on a worktree.

Also: routing every review to `codex exec review` means Claude never reviews AHKFlowApp code again. Kills `/code-review`, `custom-review-findings`, `cavecrew-reviewer`, `superpowers:requesting-code-review`. That is a very large capability loss to fix one incident, and it moves all review load onto Codex quota.

## What I'd change

- Narrow the trigger: hard boundary required only when the review target is **code in a live checkout or worktree**. Doc and plan reviews stay in-session.
- Add a **second supported tier** for Claude: reviewer subagent with `Read, Grep, Glob` only, no Bash, no Edit/Write. That is a real boundary (tool allowlist, not prompt text), cheap, and keeps Claude reviews alive. Codex read-only sandbox stays the tier for reviews that need to run commands.
- Keep everything else — snapshot pinning, manifest compare, disposable verifier, fail-closed list, cleanup path validation. That part is good and the cleanup safety tests are the right shape.
- Drop `--sandbox read-only` from the "callers cannot override" list phrasing and instead make the whole argv repository-constructed with a fixed array. Already implied; make it explicit so a future `-c sandbox_mode=...` cannot slip through `-c` passthrough. **Ban caller-supplied `-c` entirely** — right now a caller could pass `-c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access"` and the design's blocked-flag list would not catch it.

Verifier clone costs a full cold `dotnet restore` + build per review. Worth a note in the doc — reviews get slow, so verification should stay opt-in, as designed.

|---|---|---|

| 504, 502 | retry | **no** — origin may have committed |
| `TimeoutRejectedException` | retry | **no** — request was in flight |
| 408 | retry | **no** — server saw request |

Two answers.

**Once per Ctrl+A press — correct.** Hotkey fires one time per press. No repeat. Nothing wrong.

**The backtick in output — need your exact stored value.** Two cases:

- Param stored as `he said "hi" 100%` (no backtick) → output should be `he said "hi" 100%`. Backtick in output = bug.
- Param stored *with* a literal backtick → output backtick is arguable, but see below.

Paste the exact Parameters value from the UI/DB and the exact generated line from the `.ahk`.

**Real gap I hit while checking** — `HotkeyEmitter` emits `Send("...")`, hotstrings emit `SendText "..."`. `Send` applies a **second** parsing layer that `SendText` does not: it re-interprets `` ` `` `!` `^` `+` `#` `{` `}` in the runtime string.

`AhkEscaping.EscapeStringLiteral` only covers the string-literal layer. So:

| Stored param | Ctrl+A actually does |
|---|---|
| `a+b` | sends `a`, **Shift**, `b` |
| `50% off!` | `!` swallowed as Alt-modifier |
| `` 100`% `` | backtick eaten as escape, prints `100%` |
| `{note}` | `{note}` parsed as a key name |

`SendText` has none of that. #195 escaping fix is correct at the literal layer but stops one layer short for `Send` action.

Two options, your call:

1. Switch `HotkeyAction.Send` to emit `SendText("...")` — literal, matches hotstring behavior, fixes all four rows. Behavior change: users who *wanted* `^{Enter}` from a Send hotkey lose it.
2. Keep `Send`, add a second escape pass for `!^+#{}` and document Send as key-sequence semantics, not text.

Recommend 1 — "Send" param in this app has always read as text, and hotstrings already set that precedent. But it's a Wave 1 semantics decision, not a Wave 0 bug — Wave 0 gate stays green either way.

**The claim.** `CONTEXT.md` says twice that Raw *derives* its options:

PR body, in full:

```
## What

A shell command run from a worktree-isolated agent session can no longer write, move, or delete a
path that resolves under the main checkout. Closes backlog 054.

## The two-mechanism finding

Backlog 054 recorded that `git` and the `Edit`/`Write` tools were both refused from a worktree, but
a plain Bash redirect went straight through. The reason is that those are two different mechanisms.
`Edit`/`Write` isolation belongs to Claude Code itself. Only the git half belonged to this
repository. So there was nothing here to extend for Bash — the rule is new.

## The new rule

Rule name `agent-worktree-main-write`. It fires only when the session's own working directory is a
managed worktree. A main-checkout session is unaffected and may still edit, build, test, and format
in main.

Allowed anyway:

- Anything inside the session's own worktree.
- Anything outside the protected checkout.
- Build output and third-party content, on any path component: `bin`, `obj`, `TestResults`, `.vs`,
  `node_modules`.
- `<main>\.claude\worktrees\worktree-removal.log`, by exact path.

A sibling worktree is refused. It is another agent's checkout.

`AHKFLOW_ALLOW_MAIN=1` downgrades the denial to a warned allow, as it does for the location rules.

## How a write target is found

1. The tokenizer now records quote provenance per token, one character per token character. Only an
   unquoted `>` counts as a redirect, so `printf 'a>b'` and `printf x\>y` are not writes.
2. Redirects, plus a per-command destination table: the coreutils writers, `sed -i`, `dd of=`, and
   the PowerShell content and item cmdlets.
3. Nested interpreter arguments (`sh -c`, `bash -c`, `pwsh -Command`, `cmd /c`) are re-tokenized to
   a depth of 2. `pwsh -File` is deliberately not followed — the guard never reads files.
4. The target is resolved to an absolute path with every symlink replaced, so the `docs/superpowers`
   link resolves back to the main checkout. Only the leading literal prefix must expand, so
   `rm -rf ./obj/*` stays allowed. A target the guard cannot expand is denied.

## The 058 split

The second defect in backlog 054 was Claude Code's own `Edit` refusal text, which tells the agent to
edit "the worktree copy of this file". For `docs/superpowers` no such copy can exist. That text is
the harness's, not this repository's, so it moved to backlog 058 and stays open.

## Verification

- `tests/AgentWorktreeGuard.Tests.ps1` green under both pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. The
  fixture gained a second managed worktree and a real `docs/superpowers` symlink; a missing symlink
  now fails the suite rather than skipping the regression.
- Both probes recorded in backlog 054 were re-run live from this worktree session and are refused.
  Reads through the symlink and writes inside the worktree still work.
- Canonical pre-PR gate green: Release build, `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, coverage slice,
  `git diff --check main...HEAD`.
- `tests/AgentPreCommitHook.Tests.ps1` green.
```
